newsitem.title: USA: Canyon's Briggs Mine production at goal.
newsitem.headline: Canyon's Briggs Mine production at goal.

text.p: Canyon Resources Corp said Friday its Briggs Mine in the Panamint Valley of southeastern California achieved commercial production in March and April.
Gold production in March and April was 6,190 ounces and 7,079 ounces, respectively, achieving the planned average production rate of 75,000 ounces per year, Canyon said.

Cash operating costs for the two months averaged $237 per ounce. Gold was sold at an average price of $404 per ounce, using Canyon's hedge position of 245,000 ounces of gold sold forward and gold loans which will be delivered at prices averaging $402 per ounce.
The Briggs gold mine was constructed and commenced operations during 1996. The initial phase of pad construction was completed in November, the company said.

By the end of April 1997, a total of 1,630,000 tons of crushed ore, containing 57,000 ounces of gold, had been placed on the leach pad. Gold production at Briggs, since operations started, has been 24,100 ounces, including 20,600 in 1997 through April.
The company said it has been drilling additional gold reserves in the Goldtooth and North Briggs target areas, immediately south and north of the initial Briggs orebody.

It said the drilling has defined 6.3 million tons of mineralized material, with a grade of 0.043 ounce of gold per ton, containing 270,000 ounces of gold, within these two target areas. Mineable reserves in these areas are currently being calculated, Canyon said.

The success of the drilling program will enable Briggs Mine production to be increased to the 85,000 to 90,000 ounce level in 1998 from an anticipated 73,000 ounces of gold in 1997, said Richard H. De Voto, president.
